# 0.6.1 beta 7 — Independent mode controls, PID recovery and mold demand

- Give each supported Heating, Cooling, Drying, Humidifying and Fan mode its
  own method selector and parameters. Separate PID gains, sample/cycle timing,
  calibration, comfort-profile targets and supported fan/swing/quiet choices.
  Native Auto and Heat/Cool retain their valid automatic/manual choices;
  directional PID uses the individually advertised modes.
- Keep one physical actuator owner, command journal and shared device
  protections. Editing an inactive mode does not restart the active cycle or
  overwrite another mode. Preserve existing flat settings and entity IDs for
  compatibility; scoped settings are saved only when explicitly edited.
- Reset logical PID state after Resume, active intent/settings changes, policy
  pauses and unavailable feedback. Clear stale checkpoints and wake markers so
  they cannot immediately restore the pre-pause cycle. Preserve physical
  minimum ON/OFF history, valid bounded restart recovery, normal PWM OFF
  phases and unconfirmed command evidence.
- Recover an old unconfirmed native target after changed control settings and
  successful physical verification, including a new request for the same
  native extreme. Preserve minute retries and genuine manual-override handling.
  Resolve restart recovery from the selected mode's method, so an independent
  PID/Automatic setting is not left paused by an older shared method.
- Connect calibrated mold indication to actual drying demand. Use the current
  selected indoor/outdoor inputs and the existing surface-temperature
  calibration to derive the room humidity required for the configured mold
  limit. A mold estimate above its limit can now require drying while room RH
  is below the saved comfort target. Retain the saved target and expose the
  effective target, evidence and any native/room limit that prevents reaching it.
- Prevent humidification from worsening a verified high-mold condition,
  including an upstream supply wake. Missing, stale, restored or changed
  calibration sources do not authorize a mold-driven command.
- Correct humidity actuation when the appliance's local sensor is already
  below the room target but the room still needs drying. Automatic/PID with
  native ON/OFF permission uses the reported humidity minimum for drying or
  maximum for humidifying during a confirmed ON period. The qualified room
  target still controls stopping, with existing minimum operating times and
  command confirmation. Setpoint-only and Manual controls retain their
  bounded target behavior; Dry modes without a humidity setter remain
  mode-controlled.
- Apply the device's airing preference to general mold, humidity and particle
  opening announcements. A ready automatic remedy with the option off handles
  its matching problem without an opening request or wait. Preserve unrelated
  reasons such as CO₂, and keep advice for an unavailable, unauthorized or
  paused device or an invalid configured supply. Both direct AI and
  Announcement Hub receive the filtered reasons.
  A second device with airing enabled cannot reintroduce that same covered
  request or delay; unrelated problems keep their own advice and waits.
- Restore the numerical mold estimate beside its warning threshold in the
  expanded card. Show qualified mold demand and the effective humidity target
  separately from physical availability and actual appliance measurements.
- Add compact mode panels, exact native entity routing, translated mode labels
  for all 38 supported languages, and English/Greek/German mobile regressions.
  Keep known configuration available offline only for the same verified
  physical endpoints; withdrawn capabilities remain unavailable without
  causing entity-property errors.

Install **0.6.1b7**, restart Home Assistant and refresh the HEM card. Open a
device, select the desired method for each operating mode, and expand its
Parameters to adjust that mode. Existing window protection, presence policies
and physical operating minimums remain in force. This release is verified by
automated model, runtime, announcement and browser checks; live appliance
behavior still needs observation after installation. Prior releases, assets
and tags are retained.
